source.author: stat
source.text: illos e seopulis et summo vertice montis spumea porreeti dirimentes terga profundi prosequimur visu, donec lassavit euntes lux oculos longumque polo contexere visa est aequor et extremi pressit freta margine caeli.
source.text_original: illos e seopulis et summo vertice montis / spumea porreeti dirimentes terga profundi / prosequimur visu, donec lassavit euntes / lux oculos longumque polo contexere visa est / aequor et extremi pressit freta margine caeli.
source.text_english: We follow them with our gaze, as they are thrust out from the cliffs and the mountain’s highest peak, parting the foamy backs of the deep, until the light wearied our eyes as they went on, and the sea seemed to stretch long beneath the sky, and to press its waters against the farthest edge of heaven.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: it pariter propulsa ratis; stant litore matres claraque vela oculis percussaque sole secuntur scuta virum, donec iam celsior arbore pontus immensusque ratem spectantibus abstulit aer.
reuse.text_original: it pariter propulsa ratis; stant litore matres / claraque vela oculis percussaque sole secuntur / scuta virum, donec iam celsior arbore pontus / immensusque ratem spectantibus abstulit aer.
reuse.text_english: The ship, driven on together, goes; mothers stand on the shore and, with their eyes, follow the bright sails and the shields of the men, struck by the sun, until the sea, now higher than the trees, and the vast air carried the ship away from the viewers.
